Golden contracts/workflow/examples/registry-entry.json compared in Python and parsed in contract.test.ts via validateProjectsConfig from server/projectsConfig.ts (unmodified). Checks executed in this worktree: `/home/agentops/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s workflow -t .` -> Ran 210 tests, OK (a first run concurrent with `npm ci` had 2 test_automatic errors from node_modules being installed plus 1 trimmed-scan failure I then fixed; the clean rerun passed); `npm run test:contracts` -> 21 pass; `npm run test:unit` -> 130 pass; `npm run build` -> passed (existing chunk-size warning). Nothing committed.
open_assumptions: Registry merge: an existing project with the same project_id keeps its name/repository; only the workflow with workflow_id == feature is replaced or appended, other bytes are preserved. If that project names a different repository, or another workflow's runs_root equals/overlaps the new one, nothing is written and a note is printed (not a launch failure). A malformed registry (bad JSON, version != 1) blocks a live launch before any Git action. Registration happens right after `prepare` succeeds; a write failure there is reported and the launch continues.

cwd rule: the target is the Git root of the cwd (a subdirectory counts) when that root has features/; --repo pointing inside a repo resolves to its root. Detection walks up for a .git entry instead of calling git, so the dry run executes no subprocess.

'md-manager' means target == the tool's own checkout; any other checkout (even another md-manager clone) uses ~/.local/state/agent-workflows/<repo-name>/<feature>. project_id is the directory name lowercased, name the directory name, definition name 'Feature implementation' over the launched lanes.

Placeholder check scans every non-hidden file in the feature directory (including README.md) for 'TODO:'; the starter CLAUDE.md has no TODO markers and is not scanned. Scaffold lane id is 'main'; optional task sections (Context, Constraints) carry TODO lines to fill or delete.
Only reviewer prompts got an absolute schema path: no worker-completion schema file exists (1.1.0 is slice 2), so the worker completion prompt is unchanged.
The dry-run JSON gained two additive keys, 'repository' and 'registry'; commands, run directory and branch for md-manager are unchanged (asserted literally for viewer-clarity).

ClaudeSessions.run (print-mode worker in sessions.py) was kept: it is not part of the standalone interactive flow the PRD names. Removed from interactive.py after confirming nothing reachable from python -m workflow (pipeline, automatic, start --herdr, attach panes) calls them: build_interactive_graph, merge_lanes, InteractiveSessions.status, the --reuse-observers branch, and the prepare/run/status/attach CLI actions.

`status` was not run on real run directories because it rewrites report.html in runtime evidence. On copies it fails the same way with old and new code (the relocated worktree paths don't match the plan). `export` on copies matched the old code.
The README's one-time `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` acceptance step follows the PRD; it was not verified live.

findings.message: workflow/registry.py register/write_atomic: the read-merge-replace sequence holds no lock, so two concurrent live launches (e.g. two features of the same target started in parallel Herdr tabs) can each read the old file and the later os.replace silently drops the other's workflow. os.replace also replaces a symlinked projects.json (dotfiles-managed config) with a regular file. The overlap check uses os.path.normpath only, while the server's assertCanonicalRoots also resolves realpath aliases, so a symlinked runs root can pass the Python check and then fail server startup. Consider an flock on a sibling lock file, writing through the resolved path, and resolving roots before comparing.
findings.requirement: - Registry: the format is `server/projectsConfig.ts` (read it; do not edit it). The live file is `~/.config/md-manager/projects.json`; tests must never touch it, so the path is always injectable. The graph definition comes from `export_state.definition`.

findings.message: workflow/launch.py main -> registry_entry(repo, feature, runs_root, selected) calls export_state.definition(lanes, None), with no previous definition and only the lanes selected by --workers. A subset launch replaces the registered workflow's definition with a narrower graph, and any relaunch overwrites operator-customised labels that definition(..., previous) would otherwise keep verbatim. Consider building the entry from all declared lanes and passing the existing workflow entry as `previous`.
findings.requirement: - Registry: the format is `server/projectsConfig.ts` (read it; do not edit it). The live file is `~/.config/md-manager/projects.json`; tests must never touch it, so the path is always injectable. The graph definition comes from `export_state.definition`.

findings.message: workflow/launch.py placeholders(): the `TODO:` refusal scans every non-hidden file under the feature directory recursively, including README.md and reviewer briefs, not just the files init scaffolds. Any legitimate mention of the literal `TODO:` blocks the launch; for example, a slice 2 feature README that quotes the PRD's placeholder rule would refuse md-manager's own feature. This is recorded as an open assumption. Limiting the scan to the scaffolded files (feature.json, policy.json, the task files, README.md) or to lines that begin with the marker would avoid false refusals.

No test checks the prompt changes. Nothing asserts that `completion_protocol_prompt` names the tool's absolute `reviewCompletion.schema.json` path (`REVIEW_COMPLETION_SCHEMA`, workflow/automatic.py:190,229). Nothing asserts that `workflow/prompts/review.md` and the automatic prompts are free of "this checkout" and md-manager wording. `test_automatic.py:267-298` only checks enums, tokens, paths and lane vocabulary, and would still pass if the schema path were relative or pointed at the target. `BuiltinBriefs` checks only `prompts/reviewers/*.md` for md-manager-specific terms, not `prompts/review.md`. Today the file is clean (a grep found no md-manager, checkout, browser or Playwright), but no test would catch a regression.
findings.requirement: - Prompts naming "this checkout" or this repository: `workflow/automatic.py` (`completion_prompt`, `review_prompt`, `completion_protocol_prompt`) and `workflow/prompts/review.md`.

findings.message: No test covers the documentation requirement. `Trimmed.test_trimmed_files_are_gone_and_old_runs_still_export` only checks that non-test files in workflow/ and contracts/workflow/ no longer mention deleted names. It does not check that workflow/README.md has a "Use it in another project" section, or that RUNBOOK.md absorbed the folded procedures. This is a docs acceptance item, not a section 6 scenario, so it is recorded as untested rather than blocking.
findings.requirement: `workflow/README.md` has a "Use it in another project" section, and `workflow/RUNBOOK.md` absorbs the procedures from the folded docs; no remaining reference in `workflow/` or `contracts/workflow/` points at a deleted file.

open_assumptions: Registry merge: an existing project with the same project_id keeps its name/repository; only the workflow with workflow_id == feature is replaced or appended, other bytes are preserved. If that project names a different repository, or another workflow's runs_root equals/overlaps the new one, nothing is written and a note is printed (not a launch failure). Registration happens right after `prepare` succeeds; a write failure there is reported and the launch continues.
